name: TDA2822M
description: Dual (stereo) low-voltage class-AB audio power amplifier in 8-lead Minidip (DIP-8), running from as little as 1.8V. Usable as a stereo pair or wired as a single bridge/BTL amp for more power into one speaker. A jellybean of portable cassette/radio designs.

pins.name: GND
pins.description: ground / negative supply (also the thermal reference pin)

DIP-8.notes: ST documents only the 8-lead Minidip (DIP-8). Note the inputs are split oddly: ch1 inputs on pins 7/8, ch2 inputs on pins 5/6, outputs on pins 1 (ch1) and 3 (ch2).

extra.Po stereo: ~380mW/ch into 8 ohm at 6V, d=10%; ~1W/ch into 8 ohm at 9V
extra.Po bridge: ~1.35W into 8 ohm at 6V; ~2W into 8 ohm at 9V

typical_application: Stereo amp for portable cassette players/radios: each channel non-inverting, input AC-coupled via 100uF, output via 470uF to a 4-8 ohm speaker with a 4.7R + 0.1uF Zobel network. Or wire as a single BTL/bridge amp (~1.35W into 8 ohm at 6V) for one louder speaker. Battery-friendly down to 1.8V.
gotchas: ST documents only the DIP-8 Minidip; clone 'TDA2822D' SOP-8 SMD parts keep the pin order but are not ST silicon, so verify the vendor datasheet for SMD use
input pins are paired unintuitively (ch1 = 7/8, ch2 = 5/6, outputs = 1 and 3); easy to miswire
no negative rail: pin 2 is +Vs, pin 4 is GND
most cheap '2822' modules use clone silicon; the genuine ST part is obsolete
